solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Change character of versatile Durante by removal of all but tip of schnozzle

indicators.note: versatile suggests something able to take many forms, so the letters of the comedian's name are rearranged

indicators.text: by removal of all but tip of
indicators.note: removing everything except the tip of the word schnozzle leaves just its final letter

explanation.surface: A joke about the comedian Jimmy Durante, famous for his huge nose, being remade by having all but its tip cut away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'versatile' rearranges DURANTE; 'by removal of all but tip of' keeps only the end letter E of 'schnozzle' (slang for a nose, Durante's trademark).
explanation.definitionFit: To denature something is to alter its essential nature or properties, a change of character.

clue.text: Title-holder? I'm useful in a fistfight

definitions.meaning: a nobleman of the highest rank holds a title
slang for fists, so one fist speaks of its use in a fight

explanation.surface: A riddle in which a speaker claims a title and boasts of being handy in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up your dukes' means raise your fists: 'dukes' is old slang for fists.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer holding the top rank of nobility is a title-holder; slang also gives the word for a fist.

clue.text: Medieval feudal tax set up to establish regal power

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: MED is a standard abbreviation of medieval
an aid was a payment a vassal owed his lord under feudalism

explanation.surface: A history note: a medieval levy raised to secure a king's authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns MEDAID upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown or jewelled headband symbolises royal authority, so it stands for regal power by metonymy.

clue.text: Break down commercial in less than 60 minutes?

indicators.note: in places the advert inside the shortened unit of angle
less than says the unit is cut short by a letter

parts.note: in angle measurement sixty minutes make one degree
a commercial is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: Something that decomposes within the hour, or a TV commercial shorter than an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: '60 minutes' looks like an hour of time, but it is a degree of arc; 'less than' trims it to DEGRE before AD goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade is to decompose chemically or biologically, which is to break down.

clue.text: In itself, it comes between 3 and 13

definitions.text: In itself, it comes between 3 and 13

parts.words: In itself, it comes between 3 and 13
parts.note: the answers to 3 down and 13 across are word-book neighbours, and the book listing them also lists its own name between them

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about something falling between two numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is DIADEM and 13 is DINE OUT; alphabetically the answer word sits between them, and that is where you would find it in its own pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A word book lists entries alphabetically, and its own name falls between those two words.

clue.text: Best supplied towering centres in every situation — sensational!

indicators.note: in a down clue, towering means the word rises, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: supplied means fed, as in fed with provisions

indicators.note: centres in takes the middle letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: An overexcited endorsement: supplied, towering and central everywhere, simply sensational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towering' turns FED upward to DEF; 'centres in' takes E, A, T from the middles of every, situation and sensational.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to beat or overcome them, a synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Stand in line? Sit up, edging backwards somewhat

indicators.note: backwards says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Instructions to someone queueing: sit up straight and shuffle back a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Stand' alone as the definition, but the verb needed is 'Stand in'; the hidden run still starts in 'line', so 'in' belongs to the definition, not the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to act as a substitute for someone, which is to stand in for them.

clue.text: Garbage left on road in front of house

indicators.note: on means the letter for left is attached after the road piece

parts.note: a drive is the private road leading up to a house

explanation.surface: Rubbish bags put out on the driveway for collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage in the figurative sense is nonsense talk, and that is what drivel means.

clue.text: For man with great voice, dog will nurture some devotion

indicators.note: to nurture is to hold and care for, so the dog wraps round the devotional syllable

parts.note: a dingo is the wild dog of Australia
Om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hindu and Buddhist devotion

explanation.surface: A tenor's pet dog will foster some piety in him.
explanation.walkthrough: Placido Domingo is the famous Spanish operatic tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Placido Domingo is one of the great operatic tenors, so he is an example of a man with a great voice.

clue.text: Who's contracted exterminator for Slade?

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: in Doctor Who, the Daleks are robots whose cry is 'Exterminate!'

explanation.surface: Who hired a killer to get rid of the glam-rock band Slade?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who's' points to Doctor Who, the BBC science-fiction series. Slade looks like the 1970s British band, but it is an old word for a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A slade is a dialect word for a little valley or dell, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Secret affair that may be quite influential

definitions.note: describes something whose effect is felt strongly

parts.note: dark can mean hidden or secret, as in keep it dark
an affair is a matter or business

explanation.surface: A clandestine liaison that could carry real weight in high places.
explanation.walkthrough: The influence is gravitational: unseen mass that shapes how galaxies move.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers infer this invisible material from its strong gravitational pull on galaxies, so it is highly influential.

clue.text: Bullet that's hollow Daihatsu manufactured unseldom

indicators.note: hollow says each word is emptied, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A bullet that is hollow, made by the car firm Daihatsu more than rarely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' strips each of the three words to its ends: DU, MD, UM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumdum is a soft-nosed or hollow-point bullet that expands on impact, so it is a kind of bullet.

clue.text: Profound bathypelagic trends, others dismissed

parts.note: bathypelagic describes the deep sea zone of the ocean

indicators.note: every other letter of trends is sent away, leaving the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Deep thoughts on the current fashions of the ocean depths, with other ideas thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others dismissed' keeps T, E, D from trends.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deep-rooted and firmly entrenched is profound, as with a deep-rooted fear.

clue.text: Starting diet is never easy. Escape to have meal at pub perhaps

indicators.note: starting picks the opening letter of each of the next four words

parts.note: an escape is a way out

explanation.surface: A dieter's lament: starting is never easy, so slip off to the pub for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating at a restaurant or pub rather than at home is the phrasal verb's sense.

clue.text: Banks charged to make comeback with limited aim

indicators.note: the aim is limited, hemmed in on both sides by the reversed word
making a comeback means the word charged returns, read backwards

parts.note: charged as in rushed, sped
an aim is an end or goal

explanation.surface: Banks hike their charges to stage a recovery, though with limited ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb, as in 'banks on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to rely on it, and relies on is one sense of the verb.

clue.text: Gannet possibly rising to allow drop

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a gannet is an example of a bird
to allow is to let

explanation.surface: A gannet soaring upwards before letting itself plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: A driblet is a tiny quantity of liquid, a small drop.

clue.text: Extremely affectionate types showing a way in …

indicators.note: in places the article and the street abbreviation within the punctuation's name

parts.note: the ellipsis at the end of the clue is printed as three dots
RD, short for road, is a way

explanation.surface: Doting lovers showing the way in, trailing off mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis is not just punctuation: it is literally three DOTS, and 'a way' (A RD) goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: The old sense of the noun is one who dotes, foolishly fond, hence extremely affectionate people.

clue.text: What's developed in credo over time?

definitions.text: What's developed in credo over time?

indicators.note: developed suggests something worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about how a statement of belief evolves over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges IN, CREDO and T; the whole clue also describes the answer, since a body of belief grows over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of teaching or belief worked out by a church grows from its creed over time.

clue.text: I resolve to conceal theological outrage

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the verb wraps round the letter

parts.note: to resolve is to decide

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to cover up a scandal in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing a god, such as the Crucifixion seen theologically, is the ultimate religious outrage.

clue.text: Speed is quickening scorn

indicators.note: quickening means stirring into life, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Rising speed provokes contempt, as from a sneering driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quickening' rearranges SPEEDIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn someone is to look down on them with contempt, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Being involved in late rising sailors are doomed

indicators.note: being involved in means the sailors are placed within the other piece
rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors who get up late are a lost cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, as in 'the late king'; 'rising' reads it upward in this down entry, and 'Being involved in' puts the Royal Navy inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a mild euphemism for damned, so it means doomed or cursed.

clue.text: Gamble with taking lines, a product of being solid?

indicators.note: taking means holding, so the gamble word wraps round the lines

parts.note: to dice with something is to gamble with it, as in dicing with death
RY, for railway, means lines

explanation.surface: A gambler taking lines of cocaine, wondering if this is what being steady produces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solid?' plays on solidification: the answer is solid carbon dioxide.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid carbon dioxide is made by freezing the gas, so it is what results when it becomes solid.

clue.text: Is copper interrupting CID officer to indicate event in field?

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so these letters sit inside the officer's abbreviation

parts.note: DS is a Detective Sergeant in the CID, the British police detective branch
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman breaks in on a detective to point out something happening out in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman beside the CID officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the heavy disc is a field event in athletics, as opposed to a track event.

clue.text: Barnet's 'Variety' is closed and dark, unhappily

definitions.note: barnet is rhyming slang for hair, so this is a kind of hairstyle

indicators.note: unhappily signals things going wrong, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A review of a variety show in the London suburb of Barnet, sadly closed and dark.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but in Cockney rhyming slang 'Barnet Fair' means hair. A theatre that is 'dark' has no show on.
explanation.definitionFit: Long matted ropes of hair are one style or variety of hair, the barnet in slang.

clue.text: What angler holds over Wye for fish

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an angler holds a fishing rod
Wye is the spelt-out name of the letter Y

explanation.surface: An angler on the River Wye, a famous salmon river, waiting for a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wye' looks like the River Wye on the England-Wales border, but it is the name of the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The John Dory is an edible sea fish, so the name is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Attendance time not given, but learner comes in punctually

indicators.note: comes in means the learner is placed inside what is left
not given says the time letter is withheld from the word

parts.note: attendance in the sense of being on duty
L is a learner, as on a British L-plate

explanation.surface: A register-taker leaves the time out, but the trainee arrives on the dot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not given' takes T out of DUTY; L 'comes in' to the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at the proper or expected time is one sense; punctually is close in meaning.

clue.text: Fraud? Half a month before it's revealed here

indicators.note: before says the half-month comes ahead of the next piece
half takes the first four of the eight letters of the last month

parts.note: December is the twelfth month
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mid-month, a swindle is about to be exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' of DECEMBER gives DECE; 'it' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate deception of others is the essence of fraud, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Capital containing nothing grand is making a sort of bid

indicators.note: containing means the capital holds the zero inside it

parts.note: Dublin is the capital of Ireland
O is zero, nothing
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A city with nothing grand about it is bidding, perhaps for the Olympics.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a double is a call raising the stakes on an opponent's bid.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a double is itself a call in the auction, so the act is making a kind of bid.
